newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM sells 80 pct of power station.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM sells 80 pct of power station.

text.p: Base metals miner MIM Holdings Ltd said on Friday it had agreed to sell 80 percent of its Mount Isa power station to the Queensland state goverment's electricity division.
MIM said the sale was to AUSTA North West Power Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of the Queensland government's AUSTA Electric.
An unincorporated joint venture will be formed between AUSTA North West Power and Mount Isa Mines, which retains 20 percent ownership, MIM said.
Stephen O'Donnell, Executive General Manager, Mount Isa Operations, said the sale included Mount Isa Mines securing a long-term power contract.
"MIM had sought to introduce an independent operator, who would also acquire the major equity position in the power station," he said in a statement.

"This is consistent with our policy of concentrating on the core activities of mining and mineral processing and along with the arrival of gas in mid-1998, represents another step in improving the company's competitive position," he said.
The 200 megawatt power station is currently being expanded to meet future regional demand, including the Ernest Henry copper and gold mine, and is preparing for gas conversion in early 1998.
